content_preview.title: Google Open-Sources a VS Code Extension That Runs Cloud Workbench Notebooks Without Leaving the Editor
content_preview.summary: Google's new Apache-2.0 VS Code extension connects a local editor to managed Jupyter Workbench instances on Google Cloud.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Google has released a Visual Studio Code extension that lets developers run Jupyter notebooks directly on its managed cloud Workbench instances without switching out of their local editor. Announced on the [Google Developers Blog](https://developers.googleblog.com/ml-development-in-vs-code-with-google-cloud-power-workbench-extension-now-available/), the Workbench Notebooks extension is fully open-sourced, and the company is inviting outside contributions.

editor_notes.content_quality: Clear, well-structured Briefing (478 words, within the 300-800 range). Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know structure is appropriate and the piece is honest about the limits of what has been announced.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 3 source snapshots read from disk and verified; all three fetched at HTTP 200 and their uncompressed sha256 hashes match manifest.json. source-0.html.gz (developers.googleblog.com) — CONFIRMED every direct quote verbatim: 'For data scientists and developers, the ideal workflow combines the familiarity of a local IDE with the heavy-lifting capabilities of the cloud'; 'By eliminating context switching, developers can move from local experimentation to high-performance cloud compute without disruption'; 'Easily connect your local VS Code environment to managed cloud environments'; 'Run notebooks directly on Workbench instances without leaving your IDE'; 'long been a go-to platform for managed Jupyter environments optimized for data science'; 'Download the extension from the VS Code Marketplace today, and contribute to the project on GitHub'; and confirmed the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform Workbench branding. Also confirmed the article's claim that the blog does NOT state a license ('Apache' absent from the blog text). source-1.html.gz (GitHub GoogleCloudPlatform/colab-enterprise-vscode) — CONFIRMED repo description 'A Visual Studio Code extension for Vertex AI Workbench', Apache-2.0 license, TypeScript, quick-start 'Select Kernel > Google Cloud > Workbench', 'Built atop the Jupyter extension' (article: 'built on top of the existing Jupyter extension'), 'interact with other Google Cloud services from within a Workbench instance's Jupyter notebook', Open VSX distribution, and the telemetry statement 'The extension does not collect any client-side usage data within VS Code' (article paraphrase 'collects no client-side telemetry' is accurate and not in quote marks). source-2.html.gz (VS Code Marketplace) — CONFIRMED publisher 'Google Cloud (GoogleCloudTools)', version 0.1.1, description 'Connect notebooks to Workbench instances', Preview status, Notebooks category.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every direct quote appears verbatim in its cited snapshot. Every specific (version 0.1.1, publisher name, license, language, kernel-picker path, Open VSX, telemetry stance, category) traces to a cited source. concerns: The automated check flags developers.googleblog.com and marketplace.visualstudio.com as off-allowlist.
